text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Wednesday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Lithuania and Finland ratified a readmission agreement establishing the procedures for reacceptance of illegal imigrants.
- The prosecutor's office detained Rita Urbonaviciene, the deputy prosecutor of Jonoava, who is suspected of taking a 20,000 litas bribe.

- The Finance Ministry says that Lithuania's foreign debt was 3.284 billion litas ($821 million) on October 1. During the last half of 1996 the foreign debt increased by 20 percent or by 552 million litas ($138 million).
- A group of Jewish activists in Philadelphia have urged US authorities to deport a suspected war criminal, 79-year-old Jonas Stelmokas, to Lithuania.
U.S. prosecutors allege that Stelmokas served in a Lithuanian police unit during the Second World War which murdered 9,200 Jews.
Stelmokas was stripped of American citizenship last year for lying about his past to immigration officials.

- Lithuanian President Algirdas Brazauskas has signed a decree urging the Lithuanian parliament to determine its sea border with Latvia. The Lithuanian parliament will discuss the draft law at an emergency session on November 5.
